note: CAC Bank's cards page, in Arabic and in English (read 2026-10-30, no date in force given): it issues three American Express cards, Green, Gold and Platinum, billed in US dollars, against cash collateral of 120% to 150% of the limit. They are charge cards: the page says the card isn't drawn on an account directly, but a monthly bill is issued and taken from the account the customer names, so each is written as paid in full. Each card's membership terms, in Arabic, give its yearly membership fee (Green $95, Gold $175, Platinum $750, the same figures as the English page's answers; the Arabic answers give the Gold card's as $85, read as a slip against the two others) and a yearly Membership Rewards fee of $25, both non-refundable; the English card pages give the Membership Rewards fee as $20 and say enrolment is required, and the Arabic $25, stated for every card, is the one written. Supplementary cards' yearly fees ($50, $75, $350) are not the holder's own card's and aren't written. The cash withdrawal charge isn't written: the Arabic terms say interest and fees on cash withdrawals start from 4%, without the figure a withdrawal pays, and the English answers give $100 a withdrawal. No interest on a carried balance, late fee or foreign currency charge is published (the Arabic answers name a 5% commission set by the company plus the exchange commission, without saying on what, and the English answers say no commission is applied to purchases). Wave 4 (2026-10-30): no bank was added. Tried: Yemen Kuwait Bank didn't answer; no other Yemeni bank's card terms were found in the time.
